title: Winter Games
build: Epyx original, PAL, two disk sides (C64 Preservation Project, verified dump)

records.c: Figure Skating starts here: 0 into $70, the mode, which the scoring and the program's length read. The loader's file table enters this file at $1000 for Figure Skating and at $1005 for Free Skating.
Free Skating starts here: 1 into $70.

Both then start as the other events do: interrupts off, the stack reset, $083D set to say the menu was loaded over, the BASIC ROM banked out ($01 = $26), the video chip's bank 2 ($8000-$BFFF) through CIA 2, the CIAs' interrupts and timers off, port A of CIA 1 set to input, black border and background, sounds stopped, and the raster interrupt through the KERNAL's IRQ vector ($0314) at sk_irq, first at line 250. It also sets $15 to $40, which the zero-page clear in sk_setup undoes.

The raster interrupt, four times a frame. At line 124, below the crowd, it waits for the next line and stops the scroll: the rink below keeps a fixed horizontal position ($D016 = $11, multicolour on); the next is at line 192.
At line 192: background colour 2 ($D023) turns red for the judges' panel; the next is at line 241.
At line 241: text mode with the character set at $9800 (the ROM's upper and lower case set) for the bottom row, background colour 2 white; the next is at line 250.

At line 250, the top of the next frame: background colour 2 light grey; while the skater travels ($43) the crowd and flags scroll a pixel (crowd_scroll); the rink's characters at $8000 and the screen at $A000 ($D018 = $80), black background, multicolour with the crowd's fine scroll ($24) in $D016; the next is at line 124. Then a step of the sound engine (sound_step), the skater's sprites (place_sprites), the joystick (read_stick) and the frame flag at $10.
Acknowledges the raster interrupt, restores the registers the KERNAL's handler saved, and returns.

The joystick into $22, its bits turned over so a set bit is a direction held (1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, $10 fire): port 2 with one joystick ($087D) or for odd-numbered players, port 1 for the others.
Sounds stopped, the first player; then the main loop, once a frame: by the state in $11, set up the rink (sk_setup), skate (sk_run), or after the marks (sk_after).
An RTS nothing reaches.
After the marks. In practice ($081D negative) "PLAY AGAIN?" at column 20 with YES or NO beside it: up chooses YES, down NO, fire confirms; YES skates again, NO goes back to the menu.
Fire on the play-again question: YES (the Y at $A3E0) sets state 0 for another program; NO falls to the exit.
State 0: the rink is set up again on the next frame.
In competition: the next player ($71 counts from 1 to the number of players in $081E, $73 steps through their 32-byte records), one program each; after the last, back to the menu.
Back to the menu: the stack reset and the loader's $0900, which loads the menu and starts it where it left off.
The question and its two answers for print_bottom, each a column then the text and a zero: "PLAY AGAIN?" at column 20, "YES   " and "NO    " at column 32.
Prints a string on the bottom text row ($A3C0): its first byte is the column, then the characters (ASCII, which the ROM's second set shows as capitals) to a zero.

The player's name and country (16 characters from the player's record at $0800 + $73) at the left of the bottom row, spaces to its end, and, once the player has a mark, its six characters from +$10 at column 32.
LDX #60 before wait_frames, an entry for a wait of 60 frames that nothing calls; the other events have the same two bytes.
Waits X frames.
Waits X frames, then until fire is pressed, a frame at a time.
Waits for the frame flag at $10, which the interrupt sets once a frame, clears it, and steps the random number.
A step of the 24-bit shift register at random_seed: the new bit is bit 0 of $1252 exclusive-ored with its bit 5, shifted in at the top of $1250.
The random number's three bytes; the judges read the first.
The random number's middle byte.
The random number's last byte, whose bits 0 and 5 make the next bit.
unpack_list and unpack_stream, as in the other events: each stream in the list at ($16), two bytes of address, to a zero. Nothing in this event calls them; its screens are built from tables instead.

Unpacks one stream from ($14): two bytes of destination, then runs, each a count byte (0 means 64) whose top two bits say what follows: 0 one byte repeated, 1 that many bytes copied, 2 that many bytes skipped, 3 that many bytes each followed by two zeros. Unused here.
Steps the destination pointer at $12-$13, for the unused unpacker.
Steps the source pointer at $14-$15, for the unused unpacker.

State 0, a program set up with the screen off: the variables at $10-$6F cleared, the rink built (setup_rink), the player's name, the screen on, sprites 1, 3, 5 and 7 multicolour, their colours and places from the tables below, all eight on, the crowd's fine scroll at 7, the clock at 1:00.0 for Figure Skating or 2:00.0 for Free, the opening pose's move ($16D4) and frame 40 drawn. Then a wait of 20 frames and for fire, the music (sound 6 for Figure Skating, sound 0 for Free) and state 1.
For $D000-$D010: the eight sprites in four pairs, a two-by-two square at x 152 and 176, y 136 and 157, each pair a high-resolution sprite and a multicolour one at the same place; the top bits 0.
For $D025-$D02E: multicolours 6 (blue) and 15 (light grey); sprites 0, 2, 4 and 6 white, 1, 3, 5 and 7 orange.

State 1, once a frame: the clock (clock_tick), the stick on the moves (stick_moves), the frames (frame_step). When the frame count reaches $FA, which only the closing bow's last frame (a length of 255) runs down to, the program is over: its base mark (base_mark), the judges (judges), sounds stopped, in competition a wait of 10 frames and for fire, and state 2.

From the interrupt: the eight sprites' places from sprite_places, each x moved by the frame's offset ($32) and each y by the height of a jump ($2C); their pointers at $A3F8 from the base in $3A, each pair a pointer for the multicolour sprite and the next for the high-resolution one in front of it.

The shadow on the ice, drawn in characters at row 15, columns 16 to 19 ($A268), while the skater is off it: for frames 1 to 5 two characters, $75 plus twice the frame and the next; for frames 10 to 12 four, from $59 plus four times the frame; for any other frame they are cleared.

While a jump's pull ($35) is set, the vertical speed ($2D-$2E) gains it and the height ($2B-$2C) moves by the speed; when the height comes back to zero or below the ice, the pull and the height are cleared.

Counts the frame's length ($31) down. At 1, the next frame of the move's list ($42): shown, unless the list has ended or the frame a stick move is waiting for ($44) has come. Then, unless the move has been played the times it wants ($38, counted in $3F), the next move ($3C-$3D) starts at its frame $3E, or, for a negative $3E, the landing a jump earned (land_choice). A spin that reaches its count, 8 turns, ends as stick code 5 would end it (find_move): in a fall.
Shows frame Y: the sprite pointers' base swapped between $F0 and $F8 ($3B, $3A) and the frame drawn there (draw_frame).
At the count's end: the next frame's length from the list, and the list's index on.

How a jump comes down, by the fire press counted in the air ($68, from air_press). No press: land_fall, a fall. A press at or after the jump's count in land_counts: a clean landing (land_clean for a jump from skating backward, element 3 or 5; land_clean_2 for one from forward, 4 or 6); an earlier press: an awkward one (land_awkward, land_awkward_2).
In a jump's flight ($3F set): the frames in the air counted in $69, and the count at the first fresh press of fire kept in $68.
The press count each jump needs for a clean landing, by element: 82 for 3 and 5, 73 for 4 and 6 (0, 1 and 2 unused).

Each frame: in a jump's flight (element 3 to 6) the stick goes to air_press. Otherwise, once the time is up ($21), stick code 15; or, on a fresh press of fire, the directions held as the code (1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, 5, 6, 9 and 10 the diagonals), fire alone counting as 4. The code is looked for in the move's stick table (find_move).

Looks for code A in the move's stick table (the record's +2), seven bytes an entry: the code, the frames of the move it is taken in (from, to before), and either $FF and the move to start now with its first frame, or the frame at which to change ($44) and the move and frame then. A $FF code ends the table.

The stick kept as the last one, for the next fresh press. When a move answers the code, this is skipped and the last stick stays as it was, so fire still held counts as a fresh press again on the next frame.
An entry marked $FF: the new move starts at once.
The next seven-byte entry.

Starts the move record at ($2F): +4 the jump's speeds from jump_speeds unless one is under way, +5 whether the crowd scrolls ($43), +6 the element it begins ($48, counted in $49), +7 a penalty (1 a fall, counted in $46, any other an awkward move, in $47), +8 the action through move_actions, +9 the times to play it ($38), +10 and +11 the move after it, +12 its first frame. The waiting change is cleared ($44 = $FF).

The five actions of a move's +8: 0 counts cleared (act_clear), 1 the count on (act_count), 2 the element recorded (act_record), 3 the element dropped (act_drop), 4 the camel spin made a combination (act_combo).
The actions' routines' high bytes, read one on from move_actions.
Action 0: the times played ($3F) and the jump's counts in the air ($68, $69) cleared.
Action 1: the times played on by one: a spin's turns, a jump's flight.

Action 2: the element in progress ($48) written to the list at $4A, then cleared. A spin (element 1, 2 or 7, from spin_turns) that has not turned exactly 7 times changes to an awkward ending: spin_out_awkward for the camel spin, sit_out_awkward for the others. The list has no bound: each element begun adds one, on from $4A, so a program of more than 30 elements runs on into the variables from $68.
The turns each element needs on its ending, by element: 7 for the camel spin (1), the sit spin (2) and the combination (7); 0 for the jumps.
Action 3, after a fall: an element in progress is dropped from the count ($49).
Action 4: the element in progress becomes 7, the camel into sit spin, and its turns count from 1.
The rest of the record: the times to play it, the next move and its first frame.
A jump's vertical speed and pull, three bytes each, by the record's +4: 0 none; 3 -1.19 pixels a frame up, pulled 7/256; 6 -1.44, 9/256; 9 -0.97, 4/256; 12 -1.28, 6/256.
The vertical speeds' high bytes, read one on from jump_speeds.
The pulls, two on from jump_speeds.
Fourteen bytes of code nothing reaches: a step of $2F-$30 and a step of $16-$17.
The opening pose, before the music: frames 40, 41, 42, 41 and 40 for 60, 10, 60, 10 and 18 frames (the list after the record), no stick table, then skating forward from its fifth frame.
The empty stick table, its $FF alone, which the moves that take no stick share.
Skating forward, round and round with the crowd scrolling: frames 34, 35, 36, 40, 37, 38, 39, 38, 37, 40, 36, 35, the glides on frames 34 and 39 lasting 30 frames, the others 8 or 10.

Skating forward's stick table. Fire alone, or with left (4), turns to skating backward at the stride's next frame 4 or 10 (mv_turn_back). Up, down and the two left diagonals (1, 2, 5, 6): a fall at once. Up and right (9): a double axel; down and right (10): a triple; each clean when pressed on the glide or the frame after it (stride frames 0, 1, 6, 7), shaky otherwise. Time up (15): the bow (mv_bow) at stride frame 4.
A fall: frames 47 to 50 and 40, getting up (the list after it); a fall counted (+7 = 1) and any element in progress dropped; then skating forward from its fourth frame.
The other fall, backwards: frames 51 to 56 and 40; a fall counted and the element dropped; then skating forward.
The turn from forward to backward: frames 57, 58, 59, then skating backward from its fifth frame.
A double axel's take-off, shaky: element 4 begun, an awkward move counted, frames 6, 47 for 30 frames (a wobble), 7, 8, 9; then the launch (mv_axel2_up).
A triple axel's take-off, shaky: element 6 begun, an awkward move counted, the same frames as the double's (the list after this record); then the launch (mv_axel3_up).
A double axel's take-off, clean: element 4, frames 6 to 9 (takeoff_frames); then the launch.
A triple axel's take-off, clean: element 6, frames 6 to 9; then the launch.
The triple axel's launch: frames 10, 11, 12, and jump speed 12 (-1.28 pixels a frame, pulled 6/256); then the flight (fly_axel3).
The double axel's launch: the same frames with jump speed 9 (-0.97, pulled 4/256); then the flight (fly_axel2).
The axels' clean take-off: frames 6, 7, 8, 9 for 6, 4, 6 and 6 frames.
The axels' launch: frames 10, 11, 12, ten frames each.
The bow when time runs out skating forward: frames 43, 44, 45 and then 46, held with a length of 255, which sk_run takes for the program's end.
Skating backward, round and round with the crowd scrolling: frames 27, 28, 29, 33, 30, 31, 32, 31, 30, 33, 29, 28, the glides on frames 27 and 32 lasting 14 frames.

Skating backward's stick table. Right (8) turns to skating forward at the stride's next frame 4 or 10 (mv_turn_fwd). Up (1): the camel spin; down (2): the sit spin; up and left (5): a double lutz; down and left (6): a triple; each clean when pressed on stride frames 2, 3, 8 or 9, shaky otherwise. The right diagonals (9, 10) and time up (15): a fall at once, so the program must not end skating backward.
The turn from backward to forward: frames 59, 58, 57, then skating forward from its tenth frame.
Into the camel spin, clean: element 1 begun, frames 13, 14, 15; then the spin (mv_camel_spin).
Into the sit spin, clean: element 2, frames 13, 20, 21, 22; then the spin (mv_sit_spin).
Into the camel spin, shaky: element 1, an awkward move, frames 13, 47 for 30 frames, 15.
Into the sit spin, shaky: element 2, an awkward move, frames 13, 59 for 30 frames, 20, 21, 22.
A double lutz's take-off, clean: element 3, frame 0 for 8 (the list after mv_lutz3); then the flight (fly_lutz2).
A triple lutz's take-off, clean: element 5, frame 0; then the flight (fly_lutz3).
A double lutz's take-off, shaky: element 3, an awkward move, frame 55 for 30 frames then 0.
A triple lutz's take-off, shaky: element 5, an awkward move, the same frames.
The camel spin: frames 16, 18, 17, 19, six frames each, a turn; each turn counts one (action 1) and it wants 8 (+9), so the eighth turn's end makes it fall (frame_step).

The camel spin's stick table. Fire alone or with left (4) during a turn leaves the spin at that turn's end (mv_camel_out); down (2) turns it into the sit spin, the combination (mv_combo); right (8) at the turn's end, or any diagonal or time up at once, falls (mv_spin_fall).
Out of a spin into a fall: frames 15, 14, then the fall (mv_fall_fwd).
The camel spin left after the wrong number of turns: frames 16, 15, 14, 13 and 59 for 30 frames, an awkward move; then skating backward from its twelfth frame.
Out of the camel spin: frames 16, 15, 14, 13; the element recorded (act_record), which checks the turns; then skating backward.
From the camel into the sit spin: frames 21, 22, 26, 23, 24, 25; the element becomes 7 (act_combo), its turns counted from 1; then the sit spin.
A record nothing points to: the combination with an awkward move counted, and its frames 20 for 15, 21 for 10, then 22 to 25 for 8 each (the list after it).
The sit spin: frames 26, 23, 24, 25, six frames each, a turn; it counts turns and falls at the eighth's end, as the camel spin does.
The sit spin's stick table. Fire alone or with left (4) leaves it at the turn's end (mv_sit_out); right (8) at the turn's end, or down, any diagonal or time up at once, falls (mv_fall_back).
The sit spin or the combination left after the wrong number of turns: frames 22, 21, 20, 59 for 30 frames and 13, an awkward move; then skating backward from its second frame.
Out of the sit spin or the combination: frames 22, 21, 20, 13; the element recorded; then skating backward.

A double lutz in the air: jump speed 3 (-1.19 pixels a frame, pulled 7/256), the flight counted (action 1), and its turns (fly2_frames); then, its next frame negative, the landing it earned (land_choice).
A triple lutz in the air: jump speed 6 (-1.44, pulled 9/256), the turns of fly3_frames; then the landing.
A double's turns in the air: frames 5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 2, 3 for 13 frames each, 91 in all.
A triple's turns: frames 5, 2, 3, 4 round again for 7 or 8 frames each, eleven of them, 83 frames in all.
No fire in the air: frame 0, then the fall (mv_fall_back).
A lutz's landing on an early press: frame 0 and 59 for 30 frames, an awkward move, the element recorded; then skating backward.
A lutz's clean landing: frame 0, the element recorded; then skating backward.
A double axel in the air: the turns of fly2_frames, the speed already given by the launch; then the landing.
A triple axel in the air: the turns of fly3_frames; then the landing.
An axel's clean landing: frame 0 (land_clean_2_frames), the element recorded; then skating backward.
An axel's landing on an early press: frame 0 and 59 for 30 frames, an awkward move, the element recorded; then skating backward.
The axel's clean landing's frame list: frame 0 for 8.

Draws frame Y into the sprite shapes the pointers' base shows ($BC00 for $F0, $BE00 for $F8): its x offset into $32, then 8 shapes of 64 bytes from the frame's packed data in frame_ptrs. Each 8-byte cell has a mask byte, a bit for each byte that follows; the bytes without one are filled, with 0 in the multicolour shapes and $FF in the high-resolution ones, so the white high-resolution shapes in front are solid but for holes where the multicolour skater shows through, and her outline has single-pixel edges.
The 60 frames' packed data, by frame number.
The frames' data addresses' high bytes, read one on from frame_ptrs.
Each frame's x offset in pixels, added to the sprites' places, so a pose can lean out of the square.
The byte draw_frame fills empty cells with, 0 and $FF in turn.

The program's base mark in tenths ($26). In Figure Skating each element in the list counts once, its value from figure_points; then 2 off for each awkward move ($47) and 7 for each fall ($46). Each subtraction is tested with BPL, a signed branch: a result of 128 to 255 becomes 0, but a penalty larger than the mark by more than 128 wraps round to a small positive number and stands. Then at most 60, and at least 4 for each element counted. So 19 to 28 falls with no element give exactly 60, a 6.0 from every judge (tested live with 22). In Free Skating (free_mark) each counts up to three times.

Free Skating: each element up to three times, its value from free_points; then 2 off for each awkward move, and 5 for each fall and one more, since no SEC comes before that subtraction and the carry is clear. The ceiling is 60 less 2 for each fall and 1 for every two awkward moves; then at least 2 for each element counted.
Figure Skating's tenths for elements 1 to 7: 7 the camel spin, 7 the sit spin, 6 and 6 the double jumps, 11 and 11 the triples, 12 the camel into sit spin; 0 for none.
Free Skating's tenths, each time: 3, 3, 2, 2, 4, 4 and 5.
How many times base_mark has counted each element.

The clock down a tenth every six frames ($20), minutes ($1C), tens and units of seconds and tenths; at 0:00.0 the time is up ($21). Six frames make a tenth of a second at 60 frames a second, an NTSC machine's rate; on a PAL machine's 50 the minute lasts 72 seconds.
The clock as "M:SS.T" at column 24 of the bottom row.

The rink: multicolours 6 and 15, the colours of the top rows (black, light blue, the spectators' from crowd_colours, red for the flags), the rink's 224 characters copied from rink_chars to $8000-$86FF, the screen's top row cleared and rows 1 to 5 (the crowd and the flags) from crowd_rows, the ice cleared to character 0 in multicolour white, and the bottom two rows white spaces.
The rink's character set, 224 characters copied to $8000-$86FF: the ice, the crowd, the flags, the shadows on the ice, the judges' panel's letters and boxes, and its digits.
Characters 32 to 63, copied to $8100.
Characters 64 to 95, copied to $8200.
Characters 96 to 127, copied to $8300.
Characters 128 to 159, copied to $8400.
Characters 160 to 191, copied to $8500.
Characters 192 to 223, copied to $8600; the last 40 bytes are crowd_colours too.
The colours of rows 2 and 3, the spectators, for colour RAM at $D850. The character set's copy takes these 40 bytes too, as the last characters $DB to $DF.
Rows 1 to 5 of the screen: the crowd in rows 1 to 3 and the flags in rows 4 and 5, characters that crowd_scroll turns round.
Each frame the crowd moves a pixel to the left by the fine scroll ($24); after eight, the rows move a whole character (scroll_rows).

Rows 1 to 5 of the screen and the spectators' colours in rows 2 and 3, each turned one character to the left, the first character to the end, in straight-line code. The count in $25 that it takes one from nothing reads.
Row 2, the crowd, turned a character to the left.
Row 3, the crowd's front.
Row 4, the flags' top half.
Row 5, the flags' lower half.
The spectators' colours in row 2 ($D850), turned with the characters so each keeps their colours.
The spectators' colours in row 3 ($D878).
The judges' panel: four rows from panel_rows to rows 19 to 22 ($A2F8).

The marks: the panel shown, then for each of the eight judges, at the places in judge_places, the base mark plus a random -0.1 to +0.2 (unless it is 0 or 6.0), printed, with sound 9 and 20 frames when the base mark is not 0. The average of the eight (their sum over 8) goes to the player's record (store_mark) and under TOTAL, with sound 9, five frames and sound 3, the applause.
The eight judges' marks on the screen, row 21 from column 1, four columns apart.
Prints the mark in $16 in tenths as digit, point, digit at ($14) with the panel's digits (the character $BF on); 100 would print as 10.
Digit X as the panel's character.
The panel's decimal point, character $C9.
Steps the pointer at $2F-$30, through judge_places.
next_ptr's RTS, also the base show_panel reads the panel from: X runs from 160 down to 1, so the first byte it reads is $2ECB.
The judges' panel, four rows of 40 characters: the eight countries (URS, YUG, FRG, ITA, SUI, GDR, USA, CAN) and TOTAL in boxes, and the boxes for the marks.
The mark into the player's record at $0810 + $73: three spaces, the units digit, a point and the tenths ("   5.4"), and the mark in tenths at +6 for the menu's ranking.
Frame 13, upright, into and out of a spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 14, the camel spin's way in and out: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 15, the camel spin's way in and out: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 16, the camel spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 17, the camel spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 18, the camel spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 19, the camel spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 20, the sit spin's way in and out: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 21, the sit spin's way in and out: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 22, the sit spin's way in and out: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 23, the sit spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 24, the sit spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 25, the sit spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 26, the sit spin: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 27, skating backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 28, skating backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 29, skating backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 29's data on from $4000, where it crosses the memory map's edge.
Frame 30, skating backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 31, skating backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 32, skating backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 33, skating backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 41, the opening pose: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 42, the opening pose, arms out: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 43, the bow: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 44, the bow: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 45, the bow: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 46, the bow, kneeling with arms up: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 57, the turn between forward and backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 58, the turn between forward and backward: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).
Frame 59, the turn, and the wobble of a shaky spin or landing: eight sprite shapes of eight 8-byte cells, each cell a mask byte and the bytes it marks (draw_frame).

The sound engine's six slots, 32 bytes each, a sound playing in each: +0 the SID voice it plays on (0 to 2), bit 7 set when the slot is idle; +1-2 the script's address; +3 the frames until its next step; +4 a loop count; +5-6 its return stack's pointer; +8 to +14 its copy of the voice's seven registers (frequency, pulse width, control, attack-decay, sustain-release); +15 a flag that restarts the envelope; +16 its transposition; +17 a fine tuning; +18-21 a frequency slide (step, count, rate); +22-25 a pulse-width sweep (step, period, count). The file holds leftover bytes here, which stop_all clears.
Slot 0's script address (+1 and +2), the base start_sound writes each slot's through.
The script address's high byte.
Slot 0's count of frames to its next step (+3).
Slot 0's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep (+16 to +25), which start_sound clears for the slot it starts.
Slots 2 and 3.
Slots 4 and 5.
The slot count of sound_step's loops.
One byte for each SID voice: set once a slot has written the voice this frame, so a slot numbered higher wins a voice over a lower one.
Voice 1's claim.
Voice 2's claim.
Nonzero while the engine runs; start_sound clears it while it writes a slot.
The filter's registers, copied to $D415-$D418 every frame: the cutoff's low and high bytes, the resonance and the voices filtered, the filter mode and the volume.
The cutoff's high byte, for $D416.
The resonance and the voices filtered, for $D417.
The filter mode and the volume, for $D418.
The six slots' return stacks for the scripts' calls, 16 bytes each.
start_sound's copies of X and Y.
start_sound's copy of Y.
Three bytes nothing reads.
The counters of the two arpeggio routines at $50DC and $50FE, which nothing calls.
The second arpeggio routine's counter.
The S key's switch: a press sets it to 1 when it is 0, and clears it, stopping every sound, when it is not; nothing else reads it. The file holds $01 here, so the first press stops the sounds.

Starts sound A (100 and above are ignored) from snd_table: its first byte is the slot it plays in, its second the SID voice; the slot's script starts at its third byte on the next step, with the slot's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep cleared. A sound already playing in that slot is cut off.
The S key's debounce count, 0 to 2.

The sound engine, once a frame from the interrupt. First the S key, read through CIA 1 (row 1, column 5): pressed after a release, it turns snd_s_key over. The event's start-up makes port A of CIA 1 an input (it writes 0 to $DC02), so the engine's write there drives no row; the key is seen only while joystick 2 is held down, which pulls row 1 low on the same line.
For each of the six slots that is not idle: the frequency slide (snd_slide), the pulse-width sweep, and, when its count of frames runs out, the next step of its script (script_step).
The slide: the rate taken from the count, and the step added to the frequency when it passes zero.

The pulse-width sweep: every frame the step is added to the pulse width, and turned round each time the period runs out. A slip makes it change only the width's low byte: the high byte's add goes to the low byte too, with no INY between.
The slot's frames counted down; at zero its script runs on.

Copies the slots to the SID, from slot 5 down to 0: each voice takes the registers of the highest slot that plays on it, and a slot's restart flag turns the gate off and on again to restart the envelope. Then the filter's four registers.
The SID's three voices' register addresses, $D400, $D407 and $D40E.
The voices' register addresses' high bytes, read one on from sid_voices.
Stops every sound: the slots and their stacks cleared, each slot idle with its stack pointer set, volume 15 with the low-pass mode and nothing filtered, and the SID's voice registers cleared.
The six slots' stack addresses.
Writes 0 to the SID's registers $D400-$D415.
An arpeggio: sets the slot's transposition from the next of 16 steps in snd_arp_table_one. Nothing calls it.
Its 16 transpositions in semitones.
Another, for two slots side by side, from snd_arp_table_two. Nothing calls it either.
Its 16 transpositions.

Runs a slot's script from ($82) until it waits. A byte under $80 is a note: its pitch (set_note), then a byte of how many frames it lasts, and the gate on with the envelope restarted. From $80 a command, its number in the low seven bits, through snd_commands; numbers above 28 stop the sound (cmd_stop).
Steps past a command's last byte and runs the next.
An RTS after snd_continue that nothing reaches.
A note: its pitch, its length, the gate on.
Steps past the length, then sets the restart flag and the gate on.

The 29 commands' routines: 0 set the loop count, 1 loop to an address while the count lasts, 2 start another sound, 3 call machine code, 4 jump to an address, 5 call a part of a script, 6 return from it, 7 end, 8 stop, 9 transpose, 10 tune, 11 jump to machine code, 12 a note with a pulse width, 13 a tied note (no new envelope), 14 the gate off for a time, 15 attack-decay and sustain-release, 16 the waveform and envelope, 17 the pulse width, pulse waveform and envelope, 18 a raw frequency for a time, 19 the slide off, 20 the sweep, 21 the slide, 22 the volume, 23 the resonance, 24 the cutoff, 25 the filter mode, 26 the voices filtered, 27 cutoff, mode and resonance from three bytes, 28 cutoff, resonance and routing, and mode.
The command routines' high bytes, read one on from snd_commands.
Command 11: jumps to the machine code at the next two bytes; its RTS ends the slot's step. Here the step to the second byte has no carry into the pointer's high byte.
Command 3: calls the machine code at the next two bytes, then goes on with the script.
Jumps through $84-$85.
Back from the machine code to the next command.
Command 7: the slot goes idle.
Command 8, and any number above 28: the slot's registers cleared, the gate left on with no waveform, and two frames later the end command at snd_end_byte.
Command 7 ($87), where cmd_stop points the script.

Sets the slot's frequency from a note byte: the high four bits the octave, the low four the semitone, plus the slot's transposition, from note_freqs shifted right once for each octave under 7; 15 gives the highest frequency, $FFFF, for noise. The slot's fine tuning is added.

The SID frequencies of 24 semitones from C in the top octave: C is $430F, which is 1046.5 Hz on an NTSC machine and two-thirds of a semitone flat on a PAL one, as in the opening ceremony's and the menu's tables.
The frequencies' high bytes, read one on from note_freqs.
Eleven bytes of code nothing reaches: a read, a step of the script pointer, a read and an RTS.
Command 16: the control byte (waveform and gate), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 17: the pulse width, then the pulse waveform with the gate ($41), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 18: a frequency of two bytes, then a length and the gate on.
A note's length, then the gate on.
Command 4: the script goes on at the next two bytes.
Command 1: the loop count less one; until it reaches 0 the script goes back to the next two bytes' address, then on past them.
Command 0: sets the loop count.
Command 2: starts another sound, often the other voices of a tune.
Command 5: pushes the address after the command onto the slot's stack and goes to the next two bytes' address.
Command 6: back to the address on the slot's stack.
Command 9: the slot's transposition, in semitones.
Command 10: the slot's fine tuning, added to every frequency.
Command 22: the volume, the low four bits of $D418.
Command 24: the filter's cutoff, high byte.
Command 25: the filter mode, the high four bits of $D418.
Command 26: which voices go through the filter, the low four bits of $D417.
Command 23: the resonance, the high four bits of $D417.
Command 27: the cutoff from the first byte and the top bit of the second, the mode from the second's low four bits and the cutoff's low bits from its high four, then the resonance and routing.
Two bytes the filter commands work in.
The filter command's second byte, kept while it works.

Command 21: the slide's rate (255 for every frame) and its step of two bytes, added to the frequency at that rate: the rate is taken from a count each frame, and each time the count passes zero the step is added.
Command 20: the sweep's period and its step.
A note command no table entry reaches: pitch, length, gate.
Command 13: a new pitch and length with no new envelope, the notes tied.
A pulse-width command no table entry reaches.
Command 15: attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 14: the gate off, and a wait of the next byte's frames.
Command 12: a note with the pulse width's high byte, then its length.
Command 19: the slide stopped.
Command 28: the cutoff's high byte, the resonance and routing, and the mode.
The addresses of the event's 10 sounds, by number, for start_sound. Each is a slot, a SID voice and a script.
The sounds' addresses' high bytes, read one on from snd_table.
Sound 3, after the marks: the applause, a long burst of noise on voice 0 with voice 3 switched off in the mixer while it plays, and sounds 4 and 5 with it.
Sound 4, with the applause: a bugle call on voice 1, a filtered sawtooth, C C C G C E G in the top octave, then the filter reset.
Sound 5, with the applause: a long triangle note on voice 2, then one an octave lower with its pitch rising slowly.
Three bytes after sound 5 that nothing reaches: a note and a stop.

Sound 0, Free Skating's music: it starts sounds 1 and 2 for the other voices and plays voice 0's part: the pulse bass figure (free_bass) three times, twice three semitones higher and twice more, the pulse bass (free_pulse_bass) and the triangle figure; then the same again, ending with free_bass_2. It plays once, without repeating.

Sound 1, Free Skating's voice 1: the triangle figure (free_triangle), free_beats six times, a phrase of the tune (free_phrase_a), the falling noise (free_noise); then the triangle figure, the beats and the phrase again, ending with the arpeggios (free_arpeggio).

Sound 2, Free Skating's voice 2: the ticks (free_ticks), the melody (free_melody), the second phrase (free_phrase_b), the ticks twice, the melody and the phrase again, and the closing melody (free_melody_2).
A phrase on sawtooth: free_phrase_a2, a long note and a short one, free_phrase_a2 again, and another long and short pair.
Its figure of six notes, mostly 40 frames each.
The same shape lower down, a harmony to free_phrase_a, for voice 2.
Its figure of six notes.
A pulse bass with a swept width: one note sixteen times, then one a tone higher sixteen times, 20 frames each.
A triangle figure, each note sliding down: one note repeated in long and short beats with rests, broken by quick runs.
The pulse bass figure, ten frames a note: mostly one low note, its pulse width changed on every note so its tone shifts, moving up to two others at the end.
Two long noise notes falling steeply, each after a rest.
Eight short high triangle ticks, each 8 frames and a 32-frame rest.
Four rests of 80 frames and a return, which no script calls.
A bar of four beats with a slide down (free_beat).
A beat: a short triangle note, a rest of 32 frames, then a noise note.
The Free Skating melody on sawtooth, in long phrases with rests between.
The bass's closing part on a swept pulse: eight short notes with rests on each of four falling pitches, then repeated notes, one held for 160 frames, and a last run.
Voice 1's ending: arpeggios on a pulse wave, ten frames a note, four times round.
Voice 2's closing melody on a slowly swept pulse: a long note and runs down, a scale climbing two octaves, repeated notes and a last arpeggio up to the top.
Sound 8, Figure Skating's voice 2: a triangle counter-melody that answers the tune, ending with fig_phrase_2.
Sound 7, Figure Skating's voice 1: a filtered sawtooth playing a bass note and two chord notes, 20 frames each, a waltz's three beats, round the tune's chords, ending with fig_bass_phrase.

Sound 6, Figure Skating's music: it starts sounds 7 and 8, then plays the melody on voice 0, a triangle, in 20-frame beats in threes; its opening is B flat, E flat, G, A flat and G held, the fifth, first, third, fourth and third of E flat major.
The melody's closing phrase: the opening figure twice, a trill, then the opening run slowing (22, 24, 26 and 48 frames) to a held last note. The music plays once, without repeating.
The waltz bass's closing phrase, slowing with the melody.
The counter-melody's closing phrase, slowing with the melody.
Sound 9, as each judge's mark appears: a short high triangle blip on voice 0 sliding down, two frames with no waveform, then noise.
